questions.question: During hot summer days, water is usually kept in the earthen pot to keep it cool. Which of the following process is used to keep it cool?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option **4** i.e. __**Evaporation.**__

__**Explanation: **__

 
• The earthen pot has a large number of extremely **small pores** in its walls.
 
• Some of the water continuously keeps seeping through those **pores** to the outside of the pot.
 
• This water evaporates continuously and takes the latent heat required for** vaporization** from the earthen pot and the remaining water.
 
• In this way, the remaining water** loses heat **and gets cooled.
 
• This is also an example of **cooling caused by evaporation**.

The four processes provided in the options are explained below:

 
 

 **Phenomenon**
 **Explanations**
 
 

 **Freezing**
 
 
 
• The process of changing a liquid into a solid by cooling is called freezing.
 
• In simple words, freezing means solidification.
 
• It is the reverse of the melting.
 
• The state of matter can be changed by changing that temperature (by heating or cooling).
 
 
 
 

 **Condensation**
 
 
 
• The process of changing a gas (or vapour) to a liquid by cooling, is called condensation.
 
• It is the reverse of boiling or vaporization.
 
• When a gas is cooled enough (by lowering its temperature), then its particle loses so much kinetic energy that they slow down, move closer together until they start being attracted to each other, and form a liquid.
 
 
 
 

 **Sublimation**
 
 
 
• The changing of a solid directly into vapours on heating and of vapours into solid on cooling is known as sublimation.
 
• The changing of a solid directly into vapour (or gas) is called sublimation.
 
• The changing of vapour (or gas) directly into solid is also called sublimation.
 
• The common substances which undergo sublimation are Ammonium chloride, Iodine, Camphor, Naphthalene, and Anthracene.
 
 
 
 

 **Evaporation**
 
 
 
• The process of the liquid changing into vapour even below its boiling point is called** evaporation**.
 
• Whatever be the temperature at which evaporation takes place, the **latent heat of vaporization** must be supplied whenever a liquid changes into a vapour.

questions.question: What is the term used to refer to the process of conversion of water vapour back to water?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Condensation**__ is the process of conversion of water vapour back to the water.
 
• Condensation is the change of the physical state of matter from the gas phase into the liquid phase and is the reverse of vaporization.
 
• Condensation is initiated by the formation of atomic/molecular clusters of that species within its gaseous volume—like a raindrop or snowflake formation within clouds—or at the contact between such gaseous phase and a liquid or solid surface.
 
• Vapour cooling and compressing equipment that collects condensed liquids is called a "condenser".
 
• Evaporation is a type of vaporization that occurs on the surface of a liquid as it changes into the gas phase.
 
• Freezing is a phase transition where a liquid turns into a solid when its temperature is lowered below its freezing point.
 
• Sublimation is the transition of a substance directly from the solid to the gas phase, without passing through the intermediate liquid phase.

questions.question: Solids can be classified as ______ on the basis of the nature of order present in the arrangement of their constituent particles.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**crystalline or amorphous**__.

__
 
• Solids can be classified as **crystalline or amorphous** based on the nature of order present in the **arrangement of their constituent particles**.
 
• A **crystalline solid** usually consists of a large number of small crystals, each of them having a definite characteristic geometrical shape.
 
 
• In a crystal, the **arrangement of constituent particles** (atoms, molecules, or ions) is **ordered**.
 
• It has **long-range** order which means that there is a **regular pattern** of arrangement of particles that repeats itself periodically over the entire crystal.
 
• **Sodium chloride** and **quartz** are typical examples of crystalline solids.
 
 
 
• An **amorphous solid** consists of particles of **irregular shape**.
 
 
• The arrangement of constituent particles (atoms, molecules, or ions) in such a solid has only **short-range order**.
 
• Such portions are **scattered** and in between the arrangement is **disordered**.
 
• **Quartz is a form of SiO₂ (silica)**. It has tetrahedral SiO₄ (silicate) units which are orderly arranged in crystalline quartz. When SiO2 is melted and the melt is cooled, it forms **amorphous quartz glass**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The distinction between Crystalline and Amorphous Solids:

 **Crystalline Solid**
 **Amorphous Solid**
 
 

 Shape
 The definite characteristic geometrical shape.
 Irregular shape.
 
 

 Melting point
 Melt at a sharp and characteristic temperature.
 Gradually soften over a range of temperatures.
 
 

 Anisotropy
 Anisotropic in nature.
 Isotropic in nature.
 
 

 Nature
 True solids.
 Pseudo solids or supercooled liquids.

questions.question: Water boils at a lower temperature at high altitudes, because
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the air pressure is less**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The boiling point of water is lower at higher altitudes due to the **decreased atmospheric pressure.**
 
• A liquid/water boils when its vapour pressure exceeds the total atmospheric pressure over it.
 
• Unlike Pressure Cooking where the boiling point is higher due to high pressure, at higher-altitude cooking takes place at lower** atmospheric pressure**.
 
 
• This requires more cooking time.
 
• Water boils at 212º F at sea level. 
 
• At higher altitudes, the boiling point of water decreases, which leads to longer cooking times.
 
 
 
• **Relation of Pressure and altitude:**
 
 
• Pressure decreases with increasing altitude.

questions.question: Gases can be liquified by
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Applying pressure and reducing temperature**__.

__
 
• Gases can be liquefied by **applying pressure and reducing temperature**__.
 
• The liquefaction of gas takes place when the intermolecular forces of attraction increase to an extent that they combine the gas molecules together to form a liquid state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• What happens when pressure is increased and the temperature is reduced?
 
 
• When the pressure increases, the volume of the gas decreases. 
 
• The decrease in volume brings the molecules of gas together and the space between them is reduced.
 
• Further, when the temperature decreases, the average kinetic energy of the molecules also decreases.
 
• It simply means that after the decrease in average kinetic energy, more molecules have lower speeds and fewer molecules have higher speeds.
 
• The force of attraction between molecules increases as they are moving with slow speed because of high pressure and low temperature. As a result, the gas is converted into liquid.
 
 
 
• Some of the gases can be simply liquified after cooling them to or below certain temperatures even when the temperature is very high. This temperature is called the critical temperature of the gas.
